tree.summary: The most likely cause of the low oxygen condition (82% purity) is a sieve bed or compressor issue. First, verify the oxygen output with a calibrated analyzer and check for leaks.

hypotheses.why: Low oxygen output is commonly caused by sieve bed failure according to the symptom‑cause table.

cite.quote: • Low oxygen output Sieve bed failure Compressor failure

hypotheses.why: Compressor failure is also listed as a cause of low oxygen output.

cite.quote: • Low oxygen output Sieve bed failure Compressor failure

hypotheses.why: An impeded oxygen flow condition can reduce purity, though less directly indicated for this alarm.

cite.quote: The device has detected an impeded oxygen flow condition.

steps.action: Ensure the device has been running for at least 15 minutes at the prescribed flow rate (5 LPM) before performing the oxygen output test with a calibrated oxygen analyzer.
steps.expected: The analyzer reads the oxygen concentration; note the value.

cite.quote: 3. If either the yellow or red LED illuminates after 10 minutes, perform the oxygen output test with a calibrated oxygen analyzer.

steps.action: Inspect the device for leaks in tubing, connections, and humidifier bottle.
steps.expected: No hissing sounds or visible moisture; pressure holds steady.

cite.quote: If the device is alarming and the oxygen concentration is measured at 82% or higher, check the device for leaks.

steps.action: Switch off and unplug the device, then replace the Main PCA following the procedure in Section 8.9 (including removal of filter cover, inlet filter, rear cabinet, and disconnection of wiring harnesses).
steps.expected: After replacement, the device powers on and the oxygen purity rises above the low‑O2 threshold.

cite.quote: If no leaks are found then replace the Main PCA.

steps.action: Verify the compressor is operating properly (e.g., perform compressor test per Section 8.14) and confirm no leaks remain; then replace the sieve canister assembly per Section 8.10.
steps.expected: Oxygen concentration increases to >90% (or >87% for applicable models).

cite.quote: • Low oxygen output Sieve bed failure Compressor failure

steps.action: Identify the compressor type per Section 8.14, switch off and unplug the device, then replace the compressor following the procedure in Section 8.14.
steps.expected: Oxygen concentration returns to normal levels (>90% or >87% as appropriate).

verdicts.reason: The manual requires the device to run for at least 15 minutes at 5 LPM before performing the oxygen output test (Section 6.3.5). The proposed step allows only 5 minutes and omits this critical precondition.
verdicts.repaired_action: Ensure the device has been running for at least 15 minutes at the prescribed flow rate (5 LPM) before performing the oxygen output test with a calibrated oxygen analyzer.

verdicts.reason: The manual explicitly states: 'If the device is alarming and the oxygen concentration is measured at 82% or higher, check the device for leaks' (Section 6.3.6). The action matches the cited quote.

The Main PCA replacement procedure (Section 8.9) requires the device to be switched off and unplugged before opening, and involves removal of the filter cover, inlet filter, rear cabinet, and disconnection of wiring harnesses. The proposed step omits these safety preconditions and procedural details.
verdicts.repaired_action: Switch off and unplug the device, then replace the Main PCA following the procedure in Section 8.9 (including removal of filter cover, inlet filter, rear cabinet, and disconnection of wiring harnesses).

verdicts.reason: The manual's corrective action for low oxygen output (Page 36) includes verifying the compressor is working properly before replacing the sieve canister. The proposed step lacks this verification.
verdicts.repaired_action: Verify the compressor is operating properly (e.g., perform compressor test per Section 8.14) and confirm no leaks remain; then replace the sieve canister assembly per Section 8.10.

verdicts.reason: The compressor replacement procedure (Section 8.14) requires identification of the compressor type and safety precautions (power off, unplug). The proposed step omits these.
verdicts.repaired_action: Identify the compressor type per Section 8.14, switch off and unplug the device, then replace the compressor following the procedure in Section 8.14.

audit.notes: The proposed tree combines the Main PCA verification procedure (for OPI low oxygen condition) with the low oxygen output troubleshooting path. The manual does not explicitly link these sequences; technicians should be aware that replacing the Main PCA may not resolve low oxygen output if the root cause is sieve or compressor failure. The tree should include a decision point after Main PCA replacement to re-test oxygen purity before proceeding. Safety preconditions (switch off/unplug, patient on backup supply) must be added to all steps that involve opening the device.
